articles.title: Kimi Antonelli becomes youngest F1 champion with third place in Mexican GP
articles.summary: 20-year-old clinches title with four races to go. Verstappen wins race ahead of Hamilton. Kimi Antonelli closed out with the cool command of the greats to win the Formula One world championship by taking third place in the Mexican Grand Prix, a race won after no little drama by Red Bull’s Max…
body: In taking his debut F1 title for Mercedes, the 20-year-old Antonelli has etched his name into the record books as the youngest driver to claim the sport’s crown and the first Italian to do so since Alberto Ascari won in 1953. It is Mercedes’ first drivers’ championship since Hamilton last won in 2020 and the team’s 10th.

Antonelli brought what has been a hugely successful campaign to a close as the sport’s 36th world champion at the Autódromo Hermanos Rodríguez to claim the title in only his second season in F1 and with a full four meetings still to go. Sebastian Vettel was the previous youngest winner of the drivers’ championship, aged 23 in 2010, when Antonelli was just four years old.

The Italian has been leading from the front for almost the entire season, having taken the lead after the third round in Japan. With the Mercedes proving to be the class of the field in the opening half of the season under the new regulations, Antonelli made the most of it and established a dominant lead. He won five of the first six races, outracing his teammate George Russell, who had been the pre-season favourite.

articles.title: ‘We have to tell them to go down’: Iraola responds to Isak penalty denial for Liverpool
articles.summary: Manager rues two dismissed penalty claims by referee. Iraola complains ‘if you don’t go down, you don’t call it’ Andoni Iraola said he will instruct Liverpool players to go down in the box in future after Alexander Isak was denied a penalty during Arsenal’s first win at Anfield for 14 years.
body: Liverpool were beaten by Kai Havertz’s early strike after a poor clearance from the goalkeeper ­Alisson but had two penalty claims dismissed by the referee, Andy Madley. The first, a shirt-pull by the Arsenal defender Jurriën Timber on Isak, prevented the ­Sweden international reaching Bradley Barcola’s cross. The second, a hold by Christos ­Tzolis on Cody Gakpo, was reviewed by the video assistant referee, Stuart Attwell, but rejected.

Isak stood his ground when held by Timber and Iraola claimed that counted against his team. Asked whether Isak should have collapsed in the area, the Liverpool head coach replied: “It’s a shame you ask me this question but, honestly, yes, we have to tell them to go down because they’re not going to call it otherwise.

“And then referees complain why they go down. Because if you don’t go down, you don’t call it. I think Alex is honest. He tries to go for the ball, everyone can see live straight away there is a clear, clear pull.”

articles.title: WSL roundup: Arsenal stall despite Russo strike; Chelsea’s James suffers injury
articles.summary: Arsenal salvage late 1-1 draw at home against Aston Villa. Chelsea beat Charlton 6-0 but England ace goes off early. One shot, on target and in the back of the net, was all it took for Aston Villa to reopen the wound that Arsenal had been carefully trying to stitch back up.
body: Despite almost 65% possession, 28 shots to one, and 56 touches in the opposition box to four, Alessia Russo’s 85th-minute goal meant Arsenal were only able to salvage a point against Villa after back-to-back wins in the league and Champions League had appeared to have kickstarted their season.

The worst possible scenario for a team that has struggled against low blocks arrived in the 25th minute, when Lynn Wilms found Chasity Grant, who fired low into the bottom corner. It was a hammer blow to the home team, with Villa knowing exactly what to do next: stick 11 players behind the ball and frustrate the Gunners.

Russo’s late goal spared Arsenal’s blushes a little, the forward flicking a header in at the far post from a Stina Blackstenius cross, but the reprieve delivered by Arsenal’s victories over Tottenham and Benfica has been rolled back.

The Gunners have an incredibly tricky run of fixtures coming up, with Liverpool away followed by Barcelona, London City and then Lyonnes. And, despite the back-to-back wins, they haven’t been able to resolve the problems in the final third that have plagued every performance.

articles.title: Arsenal hold on for first league win at Liverpool since 2012 after Kai Havertz pounces early
articles.summary: It was a game when Arsenal showed their ruthless side and all of the champion knowhow that they accumulated over the course of last season. They headed back to London having made a statement.
body: Mikel Arteta was in the Arsenal midfield when the club last won a league fixture at Anfield; it was in September 2012, although his memories are a little hazy given the concussion that he sustained in a collision with Jordan Henderson.

Arteta has a clear-eyed focus on retaining the title and this was an occasion for his hopes to surge. Kai Havertz’s first goal in 10 appearances proved the difference but the victory was rooted in Arsenal’s capacity to control and frustrate.

It was a tough watch for the Liverpool crowd and they bayed throughout at what they perceived as Arsenal’s use of the dark arts. Arteta’s team won 18 free-kicks and there were some soft ones – each was the prompt for an eruption from the Kop. It said plenty that Virgil van Dijk responded to the full-time whistle by sarcastically applauding the referee, Andy Madley. The Liverpool captain was booked.

articles.title: Defensive 'masterclass' and elite Rice - how Arsenal ended Anfield torment
articles.summary: Not since 2012 - when current boss Mikel Arteta was commanding Arsenal's midfield on the pitch - had the Gunners won on Liverpool’s patch. That curse has finally been broken.
body: Winning at Anfield is a rarity, especially for Arsenal. But Arteta's side were ruthless at both ends of the pitch, a tactical triumph for the boss and one that underlines his side's champion mentality.

"I love when there is something that we haven't done for many years," beamed the Spaniard, who praised his players for a defensive performance he called "remarkable". If Arteta wanted to make a statement, he succeeded.

Despite being pinned back in a first half dominated by Liverpool pressure, the visitors restricted their hosts to zero accurate shots - the first time on record the Reds failed to land at least one attempt on target at home.

"In the end, that defensive line, the way we stick together, that togetherness we have, is undefeated," midfielder Declan Rice reflected. "It's nothing I've ever seen before." Nine games in, Arsenal's title defence is going perfectly to plan.

articles.title: Antonelli crowned world champion as Verstappen wins wild Mexico City GP
articles.summary: Kimi Antonelli became the youngest Formula 1 world champion in history as Max Verstappen held off Lewis Hamilton to win a thrilling Mexico City Grand Prix.
body: Antonelli finished third to secure the F1 Drivers' Championship with four rounds to spare, becoming the first Italian world champion since Alberto Ascari in 1953.
The 20-year-old avoided all the chaos in one of the most action-packed races of the season and was hugely emotional after the chequered flag.
"We did it, we did it. I wouldn't be here without Mercedes, without my family, so I'm very grateful for this moment and it's one that will live forever," said Antonelli.
Meanwhile, Verstappen took advantage of a big fight between the Ferraris of Hamilton and Charles Leclerc on the opening lap to claim his third win in four races.

articles.title: Antonelli - the boy 'born in a garage' who became world champion
articles.summary: Kimi Antonelli was a natural driver at the age of three, according to his dad. Here's how he developed to become the F1 champion at the age of 20.
body: Kimi Antonelli was 10 when his father Marco first realised the boy sitting on his lap, operating the steering and gears, might have an exceptional talent as a racing driver.
The pair were at the Adria circuit in north-east Italy, Marco with his Lamborghini sports car team, Kimi competing in a karting race.
It was the end of the day and Marco, a former driver himself, asked his son: "Do you want to try the Lamborghini?"
Marco strapped himself and Kimi into the car, belts extended around both. Dad was in charge of the throttle and brake, his son would control the rest.

articles.title: Ravens QB Jackson to undergo surgery in new injury setback
articles.summary: Lamar Jackson will undergo surgery on his right thumb and miss at least the next four games on injured reserve, Baltimore Ravens head coach Jesse Minter confirmed on Sunday.
body: Jackson suffered the injury on his first play from scrimmage in Baltimore's 36-10 loss to the Buffalo Bills when his throwing hand was hit by pass rusher Greg Rousseau.
Minter announced afterwards that the two-time MVP would be placed on injured reserve, adding "we'll see" when asked if the issue might prove to be season-ending.
Jackson had been making his return to action for one of the biggest matchups of the season after missing the last three games with a high ankle sprain.
Matters were made worse when backup quarterback Tyler Huntley suffered a toe injury in the first half, resulting in undrafted rookie quarterback Joe Fagnano coming in as the emergency third-choice.

articles.title: Lions end Vikings’ unbeaten start as Jaguars crush Colts
articles.summary: The Detroit Lions picked up a third successive victory with a closely fought 19-15 victory over the Minnesota Vikings who lost for the first time this season. The Vikings led 7-6 at the break thanks to Justin Jefferson’s touchdown but the Lions turned things around in the second half.
body: Jahmyr Gibbs gave the Lions a lead in the third quarter before TJ Hockenson’s fourth-quarter effort put the Vikings’ noses back in front, but the decisive touchdown came when Jared Goff found Jameson Williams to grab the win.

The Buffalo Bills earned a sixth win of the campaign with a 36-10 win over the Baltimore Ravens as Josh Allen and James Cook ran for touchdowns and Allen threw two more to DJ Moore and Dalton Kincaid.

The Jacksonville Jaguars ran riot with six touchdowns as they earned a crushing 42-7 win over the beleaguered Indianapolis Colts, who suffered their sixth defeat of the season. The Colts have already sacked general manager Chris Ballard and traded away star players DeForest Buckner and Quenton Nelson, with more expected to follow.

The Las Vegas Raiders produced a fightback as they came from nine points down at the break to win 38-33 thanks to Dylan Laube’s kick-return touchdown, Brock Bowers’ second score of the game, a rare rushing touchdown for quarterback Kirk Cousins and Jalen Nailor’s catch.

articles.title: LFGibbs? Jahmyr Gibbs Powers His Way To LFG Player Of The Game In Lions' Win vs. Vikings
articles.summary: Jahmyr Gibbs led the Lions past the NFL’s last undefeated team. The Detroit Lions running back was named Tom Brady’s LFG Player of the Game after rushing for 153 yards and a touchdown on 23 carries in a 19-15 win over the Minnesota Vikings.
body: Brady, who called the game on FOX, opened his conversation with Gibbs in disbelief that it was his first time winning the award.
"Congrats, Jahmyr Gibbs! Today’s LFG Player of the Game," Brady said. "By the way, a first-time winner. I didn’t even know how that’s possible."
Gibbs gave the Lions the lead with a tackle-breaking 30-yard touchdown run midway through the third quarter.

Brady then asked about a moment after the touchdown, when Gibbs left the field and was sent back out for the two-point attempt, which Detroit failed to convert. Brady asked whether it was the most tired he had ever been on the field.
